title: The bag is already here
topic: At NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, Google Public Sector and NASA teams built a proof-of-concept AI robot that found and moved a medical bag 85 percent of the time in early lab tests, because on Mars a reply from Earth can take up to 44 minutes.
hook: Who fetches the medical bag on Mars?

treatment.logline: In a pretend Mars habitat in Houston, a one-armed robot with a curious face learns to fetch the medical bag, because the real answer from Earth is up to 44 minutes away.
treatment.cold_open: A crew member in a habitat reaches for a red medical bag on a high locker, winces and grabs her back. A reply bubble lifts off the radio and starts crawling toward a tiny Earth as a clock ring sweeps.
treatment.turn: The bag slips and flops to the floor. Some tries miss, it is one task in one lab, and no space-ready robot exists. Even when it works, the arm sets the bag down and the crew medical officer opens it and decides.
treatment.button: Back in the habitat the reply bubble is still crawling, halfway to Mars. The bag is already open in the crew member's lap and the arm blinks back at her.

hero.name: the fetch arm and its eye
hero.why: a white one-armed lab robot with a curious visor face, and its separate camera on a stand across the room that watches the hand. No earlier film has drawn either, and the eye-to-hand idea is the mechanism of the story.

scenes.vo: Picture a crew on Mars, and one of them has severe back pain. A call home for help can take up to 44 minutes to make the round trip.

draw.subject: the crew member
draw.action: sits doubled over with a hand on her back while a white gripper tip stretches in from the frame edge toward the red bag on the high locker

draw.subject: a reply bubble
draw.action: lifts off the radio dish and starts crawling across space toward a tiny Earth

draw.subject: a clock ring
draw.action: starts sweeping around Earth while the bubble barely moves

scenes.vo: So who fetches the medical bag? Look again. This is a lab at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, built with habitat mockups, and the one reaching for the bag is a robot.

draw.subject: the white gripper
draw.action: waves in and out of the porthole frame as the crew member peers at it

draw.subject: the habitat wall
draw.action: slides away to show a hull mockup on a lab floor, the Mars porthole a painted panel
draw.emotion: the crew member sits up, sheepish

draw.subject: a NASA lab sign
draw.action: swings down on its chains over the lab floor

draw.subject: the robot arm
draw.action: uncurls from its base and blinks its visor eyes open at the bag

scenes.vo: Google Public Sector built it with the robotics team at Johnson, NASA's Human Research Program and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

draw.subject: the engineer
draw.action: bolts the visor onto the robot's head, a Google Public Sector tag on her sleeve

draw.subject: the technician
draw.action: snaps a cable into the robot's shoulder and it twitches

draw.subject: a third pair of gloved hands
draw.action: seats the wheeled base and the robot rises to full height
draw.emotion: the engineer grins up at it

scenes.vo: Its first job sounds simple. Find the medical bag and move it.

draw.subject: the engineer's tablet
draw.action: flips up a task card with a drawing of the red bag

draw.subject: the robot arm
draw.action: swivels its visor to the bag and opens its gripper wide

scenes.vo: Before it touched real hardware, it practised the moves in a physics simulator, where a dropped bag costs nothing.

draw.subject: a wireframe twin of the habitat
draw.action: draws itself on in glowing blue lines

draw.subject: a ghost arm
draw.action: drops ghost bags that blink away, then tries again
draw.emotion: the engineer watches the screen, chin in hand

scenes.vo: Its brain is an open model called Pi zero, from a company called Physical Intelligence. Google fine tuned it in just 2.5 hours.

draw.subject: a glowing chip
draw.action: slides into the arm's shoulder and the visor eyes light up

draw.subject: a maker's tag
draw.action: flips over on the chip

draw.subject: an hourglass
draw.action: flips and drains in a blink

scenes.vo: Mars missions need light, low power hardware. So over two years, the team tested about 15 compact devices to run it on.

draw.subject: a row of small computers
draw.action: slides onto a shelf one by one like contestants
draw.emotion: the technician squints along the row

draw.subject: the technician
draw.action: runs a test probe along the shelf and each box flickers on as it is touched

draw.subject: the smallest box
draw.action: lights up while its battery gauge barely dips

scenes.vo: To know where its own hand is, the robot uses a camera that stands across the room and watches it.

draw.subject: a camera on a tall stand
draw.action: opens its lens like an eye and blinks

draw.subject: a dotted sightline
draw.action: runs from the camera across the room and locks onto the gripper
draw.emotion: the engineer follows it with a finger

scenes.vo: The Jet Propulsion Laboratory is adapting tools built to track satellites in orbit, so the robot can understand the room around it.

draw.subject: satellite orbit rings
draw.action: spin around a small Earth with dots riding them

draw.subject: the orbit rings
draw.action: shrink into the lab and wrap the locker until they lock on the bag
draw.emotion: the technician ducks under a ring, grinning

scenes.vo: In early lab tests at the iMETRO facility, it found and moved the bag 85 percent of the time.

draw.subject: the robot arm
draw.action: grips the bag, lifts it and swings it across to the crew seat

draw.subject: a fan of ghost runs
draw.action: sweeps across the floor behind the arm, most bags landing red on the crew seat and a few flopping grey, then the counter lands on 85

scenes.vo: That means some tries missed. It is one task, in one lab, on Earth. Google has not confirmed a space ready robot exists.

draw.subject: the bag
draw.action: slips out of the gripper and flops onto the floor
draw.emotion: the engineer winces and the arm's visor droops

draw.subject: a sticky note
draw.action: slaps onto the arm reading proof of concept

draw.subject: a dashed robot outline in a rocket window
draw.action: flickers and stays empty

scenes.vo: The goal is bigger. The robot could fetch and prepare an ultrasound, and take simple voice orders, with astronauts in command.

draw.subject: the technician
draw.action: sweeps a hand toward an empty marked spot on the floor

draw.subject: a dashed ghost ultrasound cart
draw.action: rolls in beside the arm, drawn as an outline only

draw.subject: a sound wave
draw.action: ripples from the technician to the arm, which nods
draw.emotion: the technician talks with her hands

scenes.vo: Even then, it never makes the call. The crew medical officer opens the bag and decides.

draw.subject: the robot arm
draw.action: sets the bag down and folds back, visor dimming

draw.subject: the crew medical officer
draw.action: unzips the bag and lifts out a scanner

scenes.vo: Back on Mars, the answer from Earth is still on its way. The bag is already here.

draw.subject: the reply bubble
draw.action: is still crawling, only partway back to Mars, as the clock ring keeps sweeping

draw.subject: the crew member
draw.action: holds the open bag in her lap and gives the arm a thumbs up as it blinks back
